g.title: Anonymous Internet Attacker 1 role; access details in Identified Actors Inject Input into Server Interpreters Attacker submits username `' OR '1'='1' --` and any password string to the POST /authentication Level 1 endpoint. C-02 · Authentication & Session Surface No account required No weakness linked in the register Authentication bypass via SQL injection: attacker authenticates as any existing user including privileged accounts. Under stated conditions (synthetic test data) no material business harm; technically complete credential bypass is achievable. Disclosure of customer information

Anonymous Internet Attacker 1 role; access details in Identified Actors Bypass or Forge Authentication Attacker scans the target host IP on port 11434 and receives HTTP 200 from GET /api/tags, confirming an unauthenticated Ollama API and obtaining the list of loaded models. C-08 · Ollama LLM Runtime No account required Endpoints are reachable without enforced authentication (W-001) Any internet-reachable host can invoke the complete Ollama REST API: enumerate loaded models, perform unrestricted inference, delete or replace models, and exhaust GPU/CPU resources. The embedding model nomic-embed-text is equally exposed, enabling adversarial embedding queries. No LLMForge-level rate limiting, prompt control, or authentication applies to direct API calls. Unauthorized administration and changes to protected business data Disclosure of customer information

Anonymous Internet Attacker 1 role; access details in Identified Actors Bypass Authorization to Gain Access Authenticated low-privilege user discovers the RAG admin endpoint (e.g., /admin/ingest or /documents/delete) through API enumeration. C-07 · LLMForge (LLM Adapter Service) No account required No weakness linked in the register Any caller can invoke privileged LLMForge operations (document ingestion, deletion, model management, admin APIs) without holding the required identity or role, allowing horizontal and vertical privilege escalation across the entire LLM service. Unauthorized administration and changes to protected business data

Anonymous Internet Attacker 1 role; access details in Identified Actors Access Exposed Data and Secrets The PKCS#12 keystore password `changeIt` is committed as a string literal at JWTAlgorithmKMS.java:41; any actor with read access to the repository can extract the RSA private key from the packaged `sasanlabs.p12` file using this credential, enabling offline JWT forgery for any algorithm that uses the RS256 key. C-02 · Authentication & Session Surface No account required; Public source available Secrets are committed to source instead of a managed store (W-004) RSA private key extractable from the packaged keystore using the disclosed password, enabling JWT forgery for RS256-signed tokens. Under stated conditions (demonstration keys, training app) no material business harm; signing keys are not used in production. Disclosure of customer information

Anonymous Internet Attacker 1 role; access details in Identified Actors OS command injection via unsanitized input Request data concatenated into a shell/exec argument yields arbitrary command execution. C-01 · VulnerableApp Backend (Spring Boot) No account required No weakness linked in the register Technical consequence not established. Service disruption or compromise of application data

Authenticated Internet Attacker 1 role; access details in Identified Actors Bypass or Forge Authentication Attacker logs in to the Level 2 endpoint and observes the issued session ID, e.g., SESSION-1042. C-02 · Authentication & Session Surface Regular account required Security-sensitive data uses weak cryptographic primitives (W-005) Session hijacking: attacker impersonates any recently logged-in Level 2 user. Under stated conditions (synthetic test accounts) no material business harm; technically full impersonation of any concurrent session is achievable. Unauthorized administration and changes to protected business data Disclosure of customer information

Authenticated Internet Attacker 1 role; access details in Identified Actors Bypass Authorization to Gain Access Level 3 login stores the authenticated user's role as a plaintext value in the `role_level3` cookie without any integrity protection at IDORLoginController.java:141; an authenticated user replaces the cookie value with `admin` and any downstream role check that trusts the cookie without server-side re-validation grants elevated privileges. C-02 · Authentication & Session Surface Regular account required No weakness linked in the register Authenticated attacker elevates their own role to admin by modifying the client-side cookie. Under stated conditions only synthetic roles in a training app are affected; no material business harm. Technically any role claim in the cookie can be tampered to gain administrative privileges. Unauthorized administration and changes to protected business data

Supply-Chain / Build Attacker 1 role; access details in Identified Actors Bypass or Forge Authentication Missing Container Image Signing: Unsigned container images cannot be verified for provenance — any registry intermediary could substitute them. C-10 · CI/CD Pipeline Build or dependency access required No weakness linked in the register Technical consequence not established. Unauthorized administration and changes to protected business data Disclosure of customer information

Supply-Chain / Build Attacker 1 role; access details in Identified Actors Bypass Authorization to Gain Access Default GITHUB_TOKEN Scope Not Restricted: `contents: read` at workflow root forces per-job opt-in for write scopes — minimal privilege by default. C-10 · CI/CD Pipeline Build or dependency access required No weakness linked in the register Technical consequence not established. Unauthorized administration and changes to protected business data
